method: All nine actual PNGs inspected in groups of at most two. Complete batch manifest entries, current FOR/OSB space cards and relevant author-source screenplay passages checked. EED source and original 92 pixels checked in preceding pass. No art, manifest, story or code changes.

limitations: Concept-only review; no game, native-grid, animation, collision, engineering, flood or physical-safety validation.
Static props do not prove completed rescue, payments, crop ownership, consent, proxy authorization or actual access rights.

findings.finding: Field shelter and public dirt lane have open exits independent of fenced crops; rebound boundary post and contrasting crop rows appear. Domestic hearth room has an open doorway and separate open garden wicket leading to street. Cold hearth, tools, small pouch, grain sack and two chairs are visible. Layout supports private conversation without granting access or deciding crop ownership. Rows cannot prove chronology by themselves; father debt, daughter travel/labor choice and the separate marriage household remain distinct. Public routes must not be locked by a private refusal.

Mill wheel is fenced behind the separate inspection lean-to, with open public forecourt. Measuring room has two distinct measures and notched sticks; front doorway and right-side doorway join dry paths, with the right path visibly continuing along the stream rather than into water. Tables leave a plausible side passage, but actual width and water levels require collision/elevation design. Static wheel appearance cannot certify a safe stopped machine. Generated grain trays do not clearly distinguish all sieve, husk and worn-sample evidence at gameplay scale. This depicts a proposed external addition, not a changed original game mill or repeat milling task.

Seed hut is raised with a CLOSED cord-sealed private door; sprouting sample dish and measuring stick are outside. Public bypass around it remains open and joins the shared lane without entry to storage. Food hearth occupies a separate open shelter, independently approached from the public path, with three bowls, covered pot and separate seasonal tally. Ordinary small cooking flame does not touch seed store. This supports seed/food segregation and refusal of private entry or presale without physically blocking food access. Sample sprouts and decorative bowls do not establish viable seed quantity, actual meal allocation, guaranteed harvest or capacity; sold/pledged portions, finite transition food and one-season presale must be actually accounted separately.

Well lies outside the fenced private vegetable plot; its broad public approach has no garden gate across it. Bucket/rope and two distinct baskets appear. Private plot keeps its own closed little gate without obstructing well access. Right high bridge has a continuous deck, side rails and dry public approaches at both ends; rain shelter opens toward it and holds three bells and a detached fence panel. Neither panel proves a historical obstruction was actually removed, property transferred or marriage consent granted. Public water, private vegetable land, personal marriage and gift settlement remain separate. Bridge loads, flood levels and collision widths are unvalidated.

overall: 99–102 support distinct public/private access. 101 separates sealed seed storage from public food service; 102 keeps well outside private garden and bridge route dry. All are review concepts, not inventory/state or collision proof.
